Trombonist Spiegle Willcox is playing some of his strongest music at the age of 92. His style takes us back to the days of the California Ramblers and the Dorsey Brothers. Spiegle was born near Cincinnatus, New York and took up the trombone at an early age, playing in community bands and for local dances. In 1927 he joined the famous Goldkette band for a northeast tour, playing alongside Bix Biederbecke. For the next sixty years he played trombone as a sideline to his family’s coal business. In the 90s, Spiegle has returned to his first love and plays frequently in jazz concerts here and abroad. He has recorded two CDs and was recently interviewed by the Smithsonian Oral History Project.
Woodwind virtuoso Al Gallodoro is still impressing audiences at the age of 82.

His credits include work with the Paul Whiteman Orchestra, countless TV jingles and radio broadcasts and performances with ensembles led by Toscannini and Stowkowski. Al is comfortable in classical and jazz settings and has recorded definitive versions of some of the most difficult saxophone and clarinet repertory. He currently teaches at SUNY at Oneonta and performs throughout the Central New York area.
Spiegle and Al were interviewed on November 14, 1995 in Norwich, New York by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
